title: KASAN 与 KFENCE：Kernel 内存越界和 UAF 定位
key_conclusions: KASAN is the kernel-side strong detection path for OOB and UAF, while KFENCE is the lower-overhead sampled detection path.
Kernel memory reports must be interpreted with kernel config, symbols, dmesg/console context, task/cpu context, and reproducible workload steps.
Day 39's strong-versus-low-overhead distinction maps directly to KASAN versus KFENCE.
Kernel memory bug triage must distinguish slab object, page allocator, stack/global, and driver DMA or buffer lifetime failures.
shallow_points: The article does not include real KASAN or KFENCE reports from an Android kernel.
It does not validate exact kernel config options, build steps, or availability across vendor kernels and Android versions.
It does not include runnable kernel modules that reproduce slab OOB, slab UAF, double free, page UAF, or DMA stale-buffer bugs.
It does not show a complete symbolization workflow using vmlinux and module debug symbols.
discovered_connections: Day 39's low-overhead versus strong-detection comparison maps well to KASAN and KFENCE.
Day 36's corruption taxonomy still applies, but addresses now belong to slab, page allocator, vmalloc, stack, modules, or driver buffers.
Day 33's dma-buf and shared-buffer lifecycle boundary reappears as driver DMA and buffer lifetime evidence.
Day 41 should return to app-visible Bitmap memory and reuse the native/system attribution discipline from earlier days.
Later low-memory chapters should keep kernel reports separate from memory pressure symptoms such as reclaim and lmkd.
